item.research_question: How does the addition of Germanium (Ge), in synergy with Ti, Cr, Al, and Hf, affect the oxidation resistance, pest oxidation susceptibility, and scale formation of Nb-silicide based alloys at 800 °C and 1200 °C compared to alloys without Ge?
item.material_system: Nb-18Si-5Ge (ZF1), Nb-18Si-10Ge (ZF2), Nb-24Ti-18Si-5Ge (ZF3), Nb-24Ti-18Si-5Cr-5Ge (ZF4), Nb-24Ti-18Si-5Al-5Ge (ZF5), Nb-24Ti-18Si-5Al-5Cr-5Ge (ZF6), and Nb-24Ti-18Si-5Al-5Cr-5Ge-5Hf (ZF9)
item.processing_route: Arc melting high purity elements in a copper water-cooled crucible under high purity argon atmosphere; each alloy turned over five times; samples cut to 3 × 3 × 3 mm3 and ground to 1200 grit
item.test_conditions: Isothermal oxidation in air at 800 °C and 1200 °C for 100 h; heating and cooling rates of 3 degrees per min
key_findings: Alloys ZF1, ZF2, and ZF3 suffered from catastrophic pest oxidation at 800 °C, disintegrating into powder after 1 h (ZF1, ZF2) and 10 h (ZF3).
The addition of Ge substantially improved oxidation resistance, reducing the oxidation rate constant of ZF3 from 5.6 × 10−6 g·cm−2·s−1 (without Ge) to 2.7 × 10−7 g·cm−2·s−1.
At 800 °C, alloys ZF4, ZF5, ZF6, and ZF9 followed parabolic kinetics with total mass changes of 1.8, 3.1, 0.9, and 0.6 mg·cm−2 respectively after 100 h.
At 1200 °C, all tested alloys (ZF4-ZF9) exhibited two-stage kinetics: parabolic for the first 20-35 h followed by linear kinetics due to scale spallation.
The scale on alloy ZF9 at 800 °C was approximately 1 μm thick, which is 1/50, 1/13, and 1/8 of the thickness of scales formed on ZF4, ZF5, and ZF6 respectively.
Diffusion zones contaminated by oxygen (Nbss ~21.6-32 at.% O, Nb5Si3 ~2.4-2.6 at.% O) formed below the scale in ZF4 and ZF5, but no diffusion zone formed in ZF6 and ZF9.
Alloy ZF9 exhibited the best oxidation behavior at 800 °C with the lowest mass change (0.6 mg·cm−2), while ZF6 showed the best behavior at 1200 °C with the lowest metal recession rate (3.95 µm h−1).
The addition of Ge reduced the volume percentage of the Nbss phase in the ZF series alloys compared to similar alloys without Ge.
item.mechanism: The suppression of pest oxidation and improved oxidation resistance are attributed to the synergy of Ge with Ti, Cr, and Al, which reduces the volume fraction of the Nbss phase and alters the oxide scale composition to include protective niobates (CrNbO4, AlNbO4) and GeO2. The formation of GeO2 in SiO2 creates a glass with high fluidity that can heal cracks. Scale spallation at 1200 °C is caused by stress accumulation due to the high Pilling Bedworth Ratio (2.68) of Nb2O5. The superior performance of ZF9 at 800 °C is linked to the synergy of Hf and Ge further reducing the Nbss volume fraction and optimizing the parameters δ and VEC.
item.limitations: The study notes that Ge in synergy with Al, Cr, and Hf cannot eliminate scale spallation at 1200 °C. Additionally, the direct comparison with Refractory Metal High Entropy Alloys is limited by differences in temperature, atmosphere, duration, and microstructure.
item.future_work: The authors suggest further investigation into the synergy of specific alloying additions to control the volume fraction of solid solution and stabilize specific phases to eliminate pest oxidation and scale spallation.
quotes: Only the alloys ZF1, ZF2, and ZF3 suffered from pest oxidation at 800 °C.
The Ge addition substantially improved the oxidation resistance of the other alloys both at 800 °C and 1200 °C.
The superior oxidation behaviour of the alloy ZF9 was attributed to its higher and lower values respectively of the parameters δ and VEC.

item.research_question: How does the addition of Germanium (Ge) and other alloying elements affect the oxidation resistance and microstructure of Nb-silicide based alloys compared to similar alloys without Ge and to Refractory Multi-Component High Entropy Alloys (RM HEAs)?
item.material_system: Nb-18Si-5Ge (ZF1), Nb-18Si-10Ge (ZF2), Nb-24Ti-18Si-5Ge (ZF3), Nb-24Ti-18Si-5Cr (ZF4), Nb-24Ti-18Si-5Al (ZF5), Nb-24Ti-18Si-5Al-5Cr-5Ge (ZF6), Nb-24Ti-18Si-5Al-5Cr-5Ge-5Hf (ZF9), and RM HEAs such as NbCrMo0.5Ta0.5TiZr and NbCrMoTiAl0.5
item.processing_route: As-cast alloys; Isothermal oxidation in air at 800 °C and 1200 °C for 100 h; Cyclic oxidation in air at 1100 °C for about 500 h
item.test_conditions: Isothermal oxidation in air at 800 °C and 1200 °C for 100 h; Cyclic oxidation in air at 1100 °C for a total time of about 500 h
key_findings: Only alloys ZF1, ZF2, and ZF3 suffered from catastrophic pest oxidation at 800 °C.
Ge addition substantially improved the oxidation resistance of the other alloys both at 800 °C and 1200 °C.
The mass change of the RM HEA NbCrMo0.5Ta0.5TiZr at 1000 °C was 120 mg·cm−2, compared with 0.55 and 41 mg·cm−2 of ZF9 at 800 and 1200 °C respectively.
The thickness of the scale on NbCrMo0.5Ta0.5TiZr was 1750 μm, about four times that of ZF9.
The oxidation of alloys ZF4, ZF5, ZF6, and ZF9 followed parabolic kinetics at 800 °C.
At 1200 °C, the oxidation of ZF4, ZF5, ZF6, and ZF9 followed parabolic kinetics in the early stages and linear kinetics at longer times.
Diffusion zones were formed below the scale/substrate interface only in alloys ZF4 and ZF5.
The addition of Ge reduced the vol % of the Nbss compared to Nb-silicide based alloys without Ge.
item.mechanism: The superior oxidation behaviour of alloy ZF9 compared to RM HEAs was attributed to its higher and lower values respectively of the parameters δ and VEC. The addition of Ge reduced the volume percentage of the Nbss phase. The oxidation resistance of RM HEAs and Nb-silicide based alloys improves with increasing δ and decreasing VEC.
item.limitations: At 1200 °C there was spallation of their scales. Cracks parallel to the scale/substrate interface were observed in the Nb5Si3 in alloys ZF4 and ZF5. The Nbss and Nb5Si3 in the diffusion zones were contaminated by oxygen. The Cr addition had an adverse effect on the mechanical behaviour of the scales.
quotes: The Ge addition substantially improved the oxidation resistance of the other alloys both at 800 °C and 1200 °C.
Compared with the latter alloys, the superior oxidation behaviour of the alloy ZF9 was attributed to its higher and lower values respectively of the parameters δ and VEC.
The available oxidation data for RM HEAs and Nb-silicide based alloys confirms the improvement of oxidation resistance with increasing δ and decreasing VEC
